Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good evening, and welcome to Q2 FY2027 Results Conference Call of 
Bajaj Auto Limited. My name is Dorwin, and I will be your coordinator. As a reminder, all 
participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask 
questions after the initial remarks from management. Should you need assistance during the 
conference call, please signal an operator by pressing * then 0 on your touchtone phone. Please 
note that this conference is being recorded.  
                                                I now hand the conference over to Mr. Anand Newar, Head, Investor Relations from Bajaj Auto 
Limited. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Anand Newar: 
Thank you, Dorwin. Good evening, everyone, and festive greetings to all. Thank you, everyone, 
for joining for the call today. Welcome to Bajaj Auto's Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call. On 
today's call, we have with us Mr. Rakesh Sharma, Joint Managing Director; and Mr. Dinesh 
Thapar, Chief Financial Officer. We will begin our call with the opening remarks from Rakesh 
on the business and operational performance for the quarter, followed by Dinesh, who will take 
us through the financial highlights. We will then open the forum for Q&A. Over to you, sir. 
Rakesh Sharma: 
Thank you, Anand. Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the quarter 2 earnings 
call. Thank you very much for joining us. I'm delighted to say that the Q2 performance has built 
further on the record performance of Q1. It was a festival of records in Q2, 5 of them at the 
corporate level, highest ever volumes, revenue, EBITDA, PAT, and free cash flow. I'm sure 
Dinesh will delightfully dissect these for you later. The operating environment was difficult with 
inflationary pressures, logistic complexities, and capacities getting challenged for high-end 
bikes, exports and EVs. However, some deft management ensured the record outcomes.  
                                                Before we get into the BU discussion, a quick word on key organizational changes at the front 
end. We have considerably strengthened the leadership of our international and domestic 
business to drive growth and ensure robust execution. The exports business has been till now 
led by our President. This position has been upgraded to the Chief Business Officer level, and 4 
new President level positions have been created to drive Africa, Asia, LatAm, and advanced 
markets. Similarly, in the domestic operations, the motorcycle and Chetak business have been 
brought together into one new business unit, the 2-wheeler business unit. This will also be led 
by a CBO. And the India market has been divided into 2 halves, India 1 and India 2, with each 
being led by a President level position. In the back end as well, for procurement, for operations, 
and in R&D, similar appointments have been made. Almost all appointments are now done, and 
the new organization is in play.  
                                                Now let me get into the BU level discussion, starting with exports. The BU crossed its highest 
ever volume of 7.8 lakh units in Q2, a growth of 41% year-on-year. This is the second 
consecutive quarter above 7,00,000 units. We continue to grow well ahead of the industry across 
all the regions in Q2. In Africa, the motorcycle industry grew about 35% year-on-year, while 
other motorcycle exports grew 83%. In Latin America, including Brazil, the industry grew about 
12%, while we grew 44%. In Asia, which includes South Asia and ASEAN, the industry declined 
by about 7%, while our volumes grew 5%. In Middle East and North Africa, the industry

declined about 29%, and our volumes were also down 24%. So, this signals a handsome gain in 
market share almost all around.  
                                                In the largest market of Nigeria, retails were at 30,000 units AVPM level, which is a very big 
growth over the same period last year and delivered a record market share of almost 60%. Even 
though this was a very handsome growth, the retails are still only at 60% level of the previous 
peak. The new Boxer 125 heavy-duty upgrade introduced in Africa in early FY26, continues to 
scale up quite smartly with exports up by 50% plus, and it has been instrumental in driving the 
Africa growth ahead of the market. In the all-important sports segment of Latin America, which 
is 150cc and above, our exports grew by 50%, leading to being the Number 1 in the S1, which 
is the 150 to 250cc segment. 
 
3-wheeler exports did very well, too, crossing 1 lakh units in the quarter and also growing at 
41% in H1. 2-wheeler exports from India grew 32% in H1 as per SIAM data. Bajaj Auto grew 
47%, almost 1.5x the industry. Our market share in 2 two-wheeler exports from India has 
increased from 44% in FY26 to 48% in H1. And in 3-wheelers, it has gone up from 60% to 63%, 
which means almost 1 in every 2-wheelers and 2 in every 3-wheelers exported from India carries 
a Bajaj badge. Overall, the exports business has jump shifted and sustained performance at high 
levels, moving up from 6,00,000 units per quarter levels last year to 7,50,000 units per quarter 
this year. We expect to sustain this going forward. 
 
Getting into domestic 2-wheelers. First of all, I will make a few comments on industry behaviour 
and early festive indications. Given the sharp up and down movements caused by the 
announcement of the GST last year as well as the pent-up demand, we prefer to understand the 
industry movement through a longer view instead of a weekly, monthly or quarterly comparison. 
Hence, April to August for the past and September to December for the festive period. Since last 
year's base, the festive has commenced on 22nd September. So therefore, we like to break the 
year in the halves of April to August and September to December. The 2-wheeler industry, 
including electric scooters, demonstrated healthy YoY growth of 18% in April to August. The 
150cc segment and the EV scooter segment grew much higher than the industry average and 
drove most of this growth. In the September to December period, we expect growth to continue 
to be in double digits, but it may not be as much as the April - August period due to the base 
effect. 
 
In general, the festive period is 1.25x the pre-festive period, meaning September to December is 
1.25x the April to August period. Last year, this bucked the trend and the ratio was almost 1.4 
due to the GST impact. Some positive impact of the GST still continues. And therefore, we 
expect the September to December period to be better than the usual 1.25x. And that's why I 
made the comment that we expect the September to December period also to be in double digits 
but may not be the 18% in the April to August period. Of course, we have to wait and watch. 
 
In the immediate 16 days of the festive, 2-wheeler registrations have grown by 10% as per the 
VAHAN portal. As has been the trend earlier this year, this growth has almost entirely been 
driven by the 150cc plus motorcycle segment and the EV scooters. These, in our estimates have 
grown at 24% in these 16 days, even while the overall 2-wheeler growth is 10%. Our comparable

growth in this period of 16 days has been 32%, meaning 8 percentage points more than what the 
industry has grown by. We find ourselves very well positioned in both the 150cc plus motorcycle 
segment and the EV scooter segment, not just with pulsars and Chetaks, but also, I would like 
to remind you, with KTMs and triumph. And we will leverage this portfolio for growth, 
profitability and competitive position. This objective is being realized through a singular focus 
on strengthening the Pulsar portfolio aimed at the 125cc plus segment as we have been talking 
about this to you earlier. 
 
This focus is to the exclusion of the 100cc segment, where we have made a conscious choice to 
protect profitability by increasing prices due to inflationary impact ahead of competition, and 
we are accepting the consequence of this. This certainly dampens the overall volumes of 2-
wheelers, but then it also has a positive influence on our margin story. 
 
Therefore, we continue to focus our product interventions on the Pulsar portfolio during the 
quarter and even earlier. During the quarter, we launched the new Pulsar 125 and the new Pulsar 
150 in the classic range and upgraded the Pulsar 160 range, featuring several industry firsts, TFT 
displays, electronic throttled body, ride modes, projector headlamps, user-friendly features like 
Crawl Tech and traction control are bringing advanced tech within the reach of a larger base of 
customers and are driving acceptance. The new launches commenced retail in August sometime. 
The share of new launches in our 125cc plus portfolio was 7% in August. It grew to 26% in 
September. And in the first 16 days of festive, it has further grown to 33%. These new products 
launched in August onwards are now 33% in this festive period. 
 
The product pipeline remains active with further refreshes and upgrades planned across the 
160cc to 400cc range over the coming months in both Pulsar and Dominars. In addition, we will 
have 2 new brands in the pipeline, spanning the 125cc to 250cc space getting lined up for launch 
in FY27. So, by the end of festive, we hope to enter January with a completely refreshed Pulsar 
portfolio. And hopefully, the old Pulsar portfolio would have also been flushed out of the channel 
system.  
                                                Chetak, which is also now part of the 2-wheeler business units. The industry continued to grow 
rapidly at 75% plus in Q2 and penetration of electric scooters is now 25% of the scooter category. 
As we speak, Chetak achieved a milestone of 1 million scooters on the road and September was 
our largest month so far with retail stopping 45,000 unit levels and the Chetak 3503 becoming 
the highest selling model of electric 2-wheelers in India and all this despite, as you know, of 
severe capacity issues and supply chain issues particularly during September, where instead of 
60,000, we could only manage 40,000 units. 
 
Market share has moved up to 23% despite supply constraints through the quarter, which 
impaired availability by as much as 20%. Significantly, the Chetak portfolio profitability has 
moved to double digits, in fact, at an overall level, our EV business, which includes 3-wheelers 
and Chetak is now margin accretive at the corporate level. We are expanding Chetak capacity to 
80,000 per month by quarter 4, which will help us get market share and unlock new reach. Today, 
Chetak has 550-plus exclusive stores with presence in over 850 cities through a combination of 
Chetak exclusive stores and the widely spread motorcycle stores. This gives us a network that

has extensive reach and the capability to deliver a superior sales and service experience. Further 
addition of 75 exclusive Chetak stores is planned for Q3.  
                                                Coming to Probiking, which comprises the KTM and Triumph brands. The business continued 
its high-growth trajectory with 31% year-on-year growth and delivered sales of 40,000 units. In 
H1, the business unit sold 80,000 units, making it the highest ever H1 for Pro Biking. KTM 
growth was led by the Adventure and high-performance street portfolios with Adventure 350 
and Duke 250 driving the growth in their respective segments. Triumph also sustained its 
performance of 11,000 units in the quarter despite availability being impaired by as much as 
20%. 
 
Two marquee events were launched by KTM in Q2, the widely successful KTM Cup '26 version 
and the KTM Adventure Rally Extreme led by none other than the 2018 Dakar Rally Champion, 
Matthias Walkner. The rollout of joint KTM Triumph showrooms has progressed swiftly with 
120 such showrooms already operational and more in the pipeline. The KT stores, as we call 
them, now contribute to over 15% of the KTM Triumph combined volume. 
 
The adventure and high-performance street bikes are only 7% of the total motorcycle market, 
but they are growing 4x faster. We continue to lead category development and market share 
through 10 serious purpose-built models in both brands designed differently by terrain and rider 
need. This is the most by any player in this segment and positions us extremely well in this high-
growth niche segment. 
 
Moving to commercial vehicles, our 3-wheeler business unit. The business delivered its highest 
ever quarterly volumes in Q2, achieving sales of 1.62 lakh units and growing year-on-year by 
13%. The 3-wheeler category has sustained growth of 8% to 10% over the past several years 
with recent growth trending closer to 12%. 
 
In this expanding market, Bajaj Auto has maintained a strong leadership position in 3-wheelers, 
commanding nearly 90% market share now in CNG passenger vehicles and over 50% market 
share in the cargo segment. The electric 3-wheeler market continues to grow rapidly with 
industry volumes expanding by more than 100%. 
 
Bajaj WEGO remains the market leader in the e-auto segment with a market share of 
approximately 32% in September. The performance and the competitive position are a result of 
the strategy to segment this diverse market and deliver fit-for-purpose solutions for each 
segment. 
 
Consequently, the BU possesses the industry's most comprehensive product portfolio with about 
20 models across ICE and EV platforms from Riki, the E-Rick to WEGO P9018, the EV 3-
wheeler with the longest range in the industry. 
 
While the E-Rick segment has declined in H1 by about 19% due to regulation enforcement and 
upgrading, the segment is still large at 35,000 units AVPM. 10% of this is lithium-ion based and 
the rest is lead acid. Our Riki operates in the lithium-ion space and is already the market leader.

Government regulation and enforcement will continue to drive this segment towards lithium-ion 
powertrain as well as towards e-autos. We are well positioned to capture this movement.  
                                                To service the steadily growing demand, the network is being expanded and modernized. From 
just over 900 stores in FY23, the network has now grown to over 1,600 stores. Capacity 
expansion initiatives for both ICE and EV 3-wheelers are also underway as current demand 
exceeds available capacity by approximately 10%. 
 
A quick comment on spares. Spares business crossed the INR2,000 crores milestone for the first 
time, delivering robust 15% year-on-year growth. Complementing this performance, the Bajaj 
Genuine Oil business also achieved its highest ever quarterly volume.  
                                                Finally, we remain optimistic about the near and medium-term outlook. Already, our capacities 
are being challenged, as I said, in EVs, high-end bikes and some 3-wheeler subsegments. The 
overall capacity of 6,25,000 units per month is being expanded to about 7,75,000 units per month 
over the next 6 to 9 months in a phased manner. This is a new imperative in addition to the ones 
we have been sharing, which remain the same. 
 
With that, let me hand the session over to Dinesh for his update on the financial performance. 
Dinesh Thapar: 
Thank you, Rakesh. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us on this call. Before I 
begin, let me extend my festive greetings to all of you. I hope you've had a wonderful Dussehra, 
and I wish each of you and your families a very happy and prosperous Diwali in advance. Now 
coming to our results. 
 
We are pleased to report yet another record-breaking quarter, as you would have seen in the 
press release that we issued earlier today. The quarter was full of milestones. Volumes exceeded 
15 lakh units, revenue surpassed INR20,000 crores, EBITDA exceeded INR4,000 crores and 
profit after tax also crossed another INR3,000 crores. Each of these represents a first for the 
company, making this yet another milestone quarter for Bajaj Auto. Growth was broad-based 
across all our businesses, domestic and exports, ICE and EV, 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers, all 
contributing very meaningfully. So quite clearly, it was a quarter of milestones on multiple 
fronts.  
                                                That said, let me now touch upon the operating context before I get into the financials. On the 
commodities front, this last July to September quarter continued to see hyperinflationary input 
cost pressures, really with no immediate signs of these cost pressures cooling off. As we had 
indicated in our previous call, the inflationary pressure extended well beyond the conventional 
metals complex to proprietary parts, electrical components, and conversion charges and the 
escalation in these categories has continued to intensify. 
 
During the quarter, costs in electrical components increased in the mid-teens. Proprietary parts 
and conversion charges saw double-digit increases. And within the metals complex, aluminum, 
copper, nickel and natural rubber also recorded sharp sequential increases, broadly in the high 
single-digit to double-digit range. And towards the end of the quarter, as many of you may have 
tracked, steel prices also began to firm up and is adding to the cost pressures now in quarter 3. 

 
Bajaj Auto Limited

Taken together, the impact of commodity and other input cost inflation in quarter 2 was in the 
whereabouts of between 3% and 3.5% of revenue. To put this in perspective, as we had outlined 
in the quarter 1 call, the inflationary impact in the first quarter was already about 4.5% of 
revenue, 4 - 4.5% is what I had signalled then. And quarter 2 has now added a further 3 - 3.5% 
of revenue on top of that, making the cumulative inflationary pressure over the first half 
exceptionally steep, as you would imagine. The magnitude of this cost escalation is 
unprecedented, creating significant pressure on the business with inflation of a scale that we 
would typically see spread over many years. 
 
We have responded through calibrated pricing actions, which really have covered about between 
50% and 60% of the inflationary impact over this first half. The balance was largely offset 
through favorable currency realization and continued cost optimization initiatives, allowing us 
to protect margin despite the sharp escalation in input costs, which I will elaborate on as we 
move through the financial performance. 
 
We had initially expected what might have been expected to be a quarter, lasting a quarter or 2 
has now extended into a third successive quarter. And as we look ahead, these inflationary 
pressures continue to persist, and I will touch upon the outlook and our response to the evolving 
cost environment a little bit later. 
 
Apart from material cost inflation, supply chain availability has also been quite constraining 
during the quarter. The supply environment has become increasingly volatile and erratic with 
disruptions at both the back end in terms of component availability and capacity, and front end 
in terms of logistics and shipping challenges for our fast-growing exports business. In our 
electric business, supply chain and capacity constraints across both 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers 
restricted our ability to fully meet underlying demand with our plans being delivered only to the 
extent of 75% of what we had originally planned for. Having said that, the teams across both the 
back end and the front end have done an exceptional job of navigating these challenges, enabling 
us to deliver record quarterly volumes and our best ever financial performance.  
 
Coming to currency. The realization in the quarter was favorable. The rupee depreciated through 
quarter 2 with our realized USD INR rate coming in at INR95.5 versus 94.4 in the previous 
quarter and 87.1 in the same quarter last year. This sequential and year-on-year tailwind 
contributed meaningfully to our realizations and profitability.  
                                                Turning now to the financial performance. The momentum of the previous quarter has carried 
through with volumes and revenue scaling new highs. Volume crossed the 1.5 million mark for 
the first time, growing 20% year-on-year and marking the fourth consecutive quarter of record 
volumes. Revenue from operations surpassed the INR20,000 crores milestone, a solid growth of 
34% year-on-year. To put this growth in perspective, the revenue generated in the first half of 
FY27 has already exceeded the full year revenue that we reported just 3 years ago in FY23. 
 
Volumes remained the single largest driver of revenue growth. Beyond this, the revenue buildup 
benefited from richer mix reflecting the continued strength of commercial vehicles, premium 
motorcycles, exports and the steadily increasing contribution of electric vehicles. Calibrated 

 
Bajaj Auto Limited

pricing actions that I just referred to also contributed to realizations, while favorable currency 
movements provided the much-needed tailwind. 
 
On the domestic front, our electric business continues to scale up with combined 2-wheeler and 
3-wheeler volumes nearing 2,00,000 units, more than doubling year-on-year and marking its 
largest ever quarter. The portfolio now contributes more than a third of domestic revenues and 
over 20% of our overall enterprise revenues. Equally encouraging, as you heard from Rakesh, is 
the progress on profitability with continued improvement in Chetak unit economics, 
complementing the double-digit EBITDA margins in electric 3-wheelers, driving further 
improvement in the overall profitability of our electric business that continues to register double-
digit EBITDA in its entirety. 
 
Exports continue to sustain their strong momentum, delivering another landmark quarter. 
Volumes approached 7,80,000 units, translating into the highest ever quarterly export revenues 
of nearly $800 million. The performance remained broad-based with Africa reaching new highs, 
while Latin America continued its sustained run of strong performances. With exports 
contributing around 40% of our revenues, this remains a significant engine of growth and 
profitability for the company.  In addition, the spares business reached a new high with quarterly 
revenues crossing INR2,000 crores for the very first time and continuing to provide a steady 
support to the overall revenue and profitability. 
 
Taken together, the strength in volumes, improved realizations, a richer business mix have 
enabled us to cross a significant revenue milestone even as the operating environment has 
remained quite challenging. Let me now move to EBITDA and margins and how we have 
translated the strong revenue growth into profitability amidst the hyperinflationary cost 
environment that I mentioned. 
 
On EBITDA, we crossed the INR4,000 crores mark, delivering INR4,172 crores, again, a new 
high for the company with a strong 37% year-on-year growth. What is particularly noteworthy 
here is that the profit growth outpaced the revenue growth with profit increasing by 37% year-
on-year against revenue growth of 34% Sequentially, EBITDA margins held steady at 20.9% as 
we navigated another quarter of a challenging operating environment. Higher realizations 
supported by calibrated pricing action and favorable currency helped absorb a part of the cost 
inflation pressure. Operating leverage with a INR20,000 crores quarter from higher revenue, 
alongside disciplined cost management and a very hard look that we did on discretionary spend 
helped offset the remaining cost pressures and sustained our margin delivery. 
 
On a year-on-year basis, margins expanded 40 basis points with favorable currency realizations 
and really improved operating leverage being the principal drivers, more than offsetting very 
severe and adverse cost price dynamics. This improvement came despite an adverse mix impact 
from the growing contribution of the electric 2-wheeler business, which whilst getting better, 
still remains dilutive to the overall company. 
 
I know many of you are keen to understand the step-up in other operating income. It's a question 
that has been asked of in the past. And so let me address this really upfront. Now there are 3

                                                And lastly, you heard from Rakesh, in keeping with the broader growth momentum across the 
business, we've had a very good quarter on our Bajaj Genuine Oil business, which is what we 
call BGO, with higher volumes really translating into increased royalty income and contributing 
to the step-up in other operating income. So those are really the 3 factors which have led to the 
step-up of the other operating income. Export incentives, PLI accruals 3 factors for that and 
really stepped-up royalty receipts for our BGO business, which has been quite buoyant. 
 
Turning to profit after tax. We recorded our best ever PAT crossing INR3,000 crores, coming in 
at INR3,354 crores, up 35% year-on-year.  
                                                Quickly, a word on cash. Consistent with our track record of strong free cash flow generation, 
we generated nearly INR4,000 crores of free cash flow during the quarter, translating into a cash 
conversion of 100% plus of the profit after tax. This strong conversion was supported by a 
combination of robust earnings and favorable working capital movements, enabling us to 
translate our profitability into cash while continuing to fund the needs of the business.  
                                                Moving to the consolidated performance. And as I explained last quarter, the year-on-year 
comparison continues to be impacted by the change in consolidation following the acquisition 
of the control of Bajaj Mobility AG, whose financial results are now consolidated into ours, 
although with a 1 quarter lag. The current quarter, therefore, reflects a full quarter of its 
consolidated results, which was not reflected on the same basis in the corresponding period of 
last year. The reported growth rates, therefore, need to be viewed in this context.

                                                That said, from a headline perspective, consolidated revenue for the quarter came in at 
INR25,126 crores, a growth of 60% year-on-year and consolidated profit after tax stood at 
INR3,400-plus crores, also growing by 60% plus over the previous year. Alongside the impact 
of the expanded consolidation, the contribution from our subsidiaries now is becoming 
increasingly meaningful, supported by the continued scale-up of BACL the steady expansion of 
our Brazilian business and the consolidation of Bajaj Mobility AG, which essentially represents 
the KTM business. Together, these businesses are adding greater scale and depth to our 
consolidated performance. 
 
Let me now spend a minute on KTM and BACL. The recovery of the KTM business is gaining 
traction with significant improvements in both scale and profitability. Revenue grew 65% year-
on-year to EUR701 million in the first half, while EBITDA turned positive at EUR38 million 
compared with a loss of over EUR180 million in the corresponding period of last year, of course, 
adjusted with the restructuring profit. This reflects the recovering motorcycle sales, a sharper 
focus on cost efficiencies and a reduction of fixed costs. Inventory levels across the KTM system 
and the dealer network have now returned to normalized levels. In fact, in Q2, the EBIT also 
returned to positive territory for the first time since the conclusion of the restructuring 
proceedings. These are encouraging steps in restoring the business to a more sustainable 
operating footing with a focus continuing on profitable growth, cost discipline and cash 
generation. As Bajaj Mobility AG is a listed entity, its detailed financial results and other 
disclosures can be accessed from its website. 
 
BACL continues to scale up strongly, delivering another stellar quarter of robust growth and 
profitability. Total income stood at nearly INR1,200 crores while profit after tax for the quarter 
came in at INR243 crores, representing a strong growth of 85% year-on-year. To give you a 
sense of the scale of the business, assets under management are now nearly at INR21,000 crores, 
growing more than 1.5x over the previous year. The capital adequacy ratio remained very 
healthy at almost 19.5%, while the business continues to operate at industry-leading returns of 
equity of 26% as of 30th September.  
                                                Looking ahead now, on commodities, we've entered the third consecutive quarter of an 
exceptionally challenging operating environment with input cost inflation, showing no real signs 
or immediate signs of easing. The pressure continues to extend beyond the metals complex into 
proprietary parts, electrical components and conversion charges. And within the metals complex, 
steel and copper prices, in particular, are quite firm and stiff as we speak and remain elevated. 
 
While the pace of cost escalation may be lower than the sharp increase witnessed in the first half 
of the year between quarter 1 and quarter 2, the situation notwithstanding remains highly 
dynamic, and it's really difficult to pin down a number for the inflationary impact at this stage. 
So therefore, we're seeing the quarter as being one of inflation, but the magnitude of that inflation 
as things currently stand because of the many moving parts is very hard to put out at this stage. 
 
We have, though, taken some level of calibrated pricing earlier this month to recover a third of 
the inflationary impact so far. Going forward, of course, we will need to carefully assess the 
market's ability to absorb further pricing, particularly as we navigate this third consecutive
